title: Power Circuit Arcade
intro: Six rounds on voltage, current, resistance and how ARIA's power loop holds together. Get them right first try to earn ⭐⭐⭐!

rounds.prompt: In the water analogy, what does tank height stand in for?
rounds.explain: A taller tank pushes harder, exactly like a higher voltage pushes current harder through a circuit.

rounds.prompt: Match each electrical quantity to its water twin.

pairs.right: A valve you open or close

rounds.explain: Four ideas, four water twins. Once the pairing sticks, Ohm's law is just describing the plumbing.

rounds.prompt: A 9V circuit has a 450Ω resistor. Using I = V/R, about how much current flows?
rounds.explain: 9 ÷ 450 = 0.02 A = 20 mA. Dividing volts by ohms always gives you amps.

rounds.prompt: You accidentally bridge a bare wire straight across your LED. What happens?
options: Current takes the easy shortcut and skips the LED entirely, which stays dark
rounds.explain: That's a short circuit: an easier path that bypasses your part. Current always takes the path of least resistance.

rounds.prompt: Why does flipping an LED backwards leave it dark, when flipping a resistor backwards changes nothing?
options: An LED only conducts current in one direction; a resistor doesn't care about direction
LEDs are more fragile than resistors
Backwards LEDs need more voltage, not less
rounds.explain: An LED is a one-way valve for current. A resistor just resists — it works the same wired either way.

rounds.prompt: Two identical LEDs, wired in parallel instead of series. What changes?
options: Each LED shines brighter, but the battery supplies more total current
rounds.explain: Parallel gives each LED its own full-voltage path, so each burns brighter — at the cost of drawing more total current from the battery.
